subject: HelixPay: benchmark checkpoint & runbook (acceptance criteria + MOP)
messages:
From: Charlotte Park <charlotte@helixpay.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
Cc: HelixPay Procurement <procurement@helixpay.com>, Derek Huang <derek.huang@helixpay.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark checkpoint & runbook

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. We want to lock the acceptance criteria and get a Method of Procedure (MOP) in place so our infra team can be ready on our side. A few clarifying items from us before the run:

- Our production peak is ~110 qps but with 3x daily short spikes (up to ~320 qps for ~30s).
- We need P95 inference latency to be predictable — target is <= 300ms for our interactive flows.
- During ramp we can provide a traffic replay (sanitized) and a small set of synthetic transactions.

Can you share the runbook you intend to execute, the expected test durations (ramp / soak / spike windows), and the exact metrics Redwood will record and share? Also please include any credential or IP allowlist details required for the test environment.

Thanks,
Charlotte
Charlotte Park
Head of Integrations
HelixPay

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
To: Charlotte Park <charlotte@helixpay.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.inference>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark checkpoint & runbook

Hi Charlotte —

Appreciate the detail — attached is our proposed runbook (helixpay-benchmark-runbook-v1.pdf) and the load scripts we plan to use. High level plan below:

1) Pre-run (30 min): IP allowlist + API key test, confirm KV cache warm-up steps (we'll seed common prefixes for 5 minutes).
2) Ramp (10 min): linear ramp to target steady-state 120 qps.
3) Soak (20 min): maintain 120 qps steady-state to observe long-tail behavior and memory/KV stability.
4) Spike window (2 x 1 min spikes): two 30s bursts to 320 qps with 30s recovery, to mimic your production spikes.
5) Failure injection (opt): short 60s sim of backend timeout to validate graceful degradation and fallback routing.

Acceptance metrics we will capture and share:
- P50, P95, P99 latencies (end-to-end generation time)
- Successful response rate (2xx) and token throughput (tokens/s)
- CPU/GPU utilization and per-GPU memory trend during windows
- KV cache hit ratio and effective batching stats (avg batch size)

Suggested acceptance thresholds (Redwood recommendation):
- P95 <= 250 ms (steady-state)
- P99 <= 600 ms (steady-state)
- 99% success rate during soak

Notes: we list stricter P95 than your target to give headroom during spikes; happy to align. Runbook also contains exact curl examples and the load runner config.

I've attached the scripts and the runbook here. For the test environment we'll use the sandbox cluster at https://app.redwood.com/sessions/helixpay-testenv — we'll send temporary API keys and the IPs to allowlist in a separate secure email.

Propose we run on Tue Aug 3 2027 09:00 PDT. If that works, we'll reserve an SRE and a PM to monitor and share a results spreadsheet after the run.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: helixpay-benchmark-runbook-v1.pdf (23 pages), helixpay-load-scripts-v2.tar.gz (load scripts)

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>, Charlotte Park <charlotte@helixpay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark checkpoint & runbook

Quick tech notes from infra — a few items to confirm before the run:

- KV cache warm-up: we'll seed the top 200 prefixes. Please confirm you can provide the common prompt prefixes or allow us to replay a small sanitized set.
- Batching config: we'll start with dynamic batching with a 15ms max hold and 32 token cap per batch; if your replay has many short inputs we may reduce the hold to 10ms to prioritize latency.
- Model variant: we'll test on the v1.3 quantized variant (recommended for cost/latency). If you require full FP16 for quality, flag it now so we can provision memory.

Also, we will stream monitoring logs to the shared Drive link and create a live Grafana panel for the team. For failure injection, are you OK with a short (60s) simulated backend push to check fallback?

Ben Carter
Technical Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Charlotte Park <charlotte@helixpay.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Derek Huang <derek.huang@helixpay.com>, HelixPay Procurement <procurement@helixpay.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark checkpoint & runbook

Thanks — this looks good. A few confirmations from our infra team:

- We can provide a sanitized replay of ~1,200 transactions to seed the cache.
- We accept the dynamic batching defaults; prefer P95 <= 300 ms and P99 <= 650 ms as our formal acceptance thresholds (we'll tolerate deviations during the two brief spikes).
- Please include success rate (2xx) per minute in the results sheet and annotate any dropped requests with error codes.

Derek and I are fine with the failure injection as long as it is scheduled during a controlled window and the scope is limited to the Redwood sandbox.

We'll have two HelixPay SREs on the call: Derek Huang and Maya Singh (maya.singh@helixpay.com). If the date is Aug 3 at 09:00 PDT still stands, we'll mark the calendar and confirm IP allowlist details by EOD Tue Aug 2.

—Charlotte

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
To: Charlotte Park <charlotte@helixpay.com>, Derek Huang <derek.huang@helixpay.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.inference>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark checkpoint & runbook

Great — confirmed for Tue Aug 3, 09:00 PDT. Final checklist we will execute 60–30 minutes before run:

- IP allowlist + issue temporary API keys (Redwood security will email keys to charlotte@helixpay.com).
- Seed KV cache (we will run the supplied sanitized replay, thank you).
- Start Grafana dashboard and live Drive folder.
- Record baseline (5 min) → ramp → soak → two spike windows → optional failure injection.

Deliverables after the run (within 24 hours):
- Raw CSV of per-minute latencies + success rates (attached as helixpay-results-20270803.csv)
- Summary PDF that flags any thresholds missed and recommended mitigation steps
- Short recording of the Grafana session (uploaded to Drive)

Attendees on Redwood side: Vanessa Ortiz (CSM), Ben Carter (Tech Lead), Laura Bennett (SRE).

If anything changes on your side, flag it here — otherwise we'll run and share results. Looking forward to getting you across the finish line.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: helixpay-results-20270803.csv
